channel.title: Tech Xplore - electronic gadgets, technology advances and research news
channel.description: Tech Xplore internet news portal provides the latest news on electronics, technology, and engineering.

item.title: From Carnegie to Claude: AI wealth could reshape philanthropy
item.description: A wave of American wealth created by artificial intelligence companies could produce some of the largest charitable sums since the era of Andrew Carnegie and John D. Rockefeller, raising questions about where the money goes.

item.title: Data center next door divides old Massachusetts mill town
item.description: Retiree Eileen Castle hasn't been able to enjoy her backyard since a data center moved in next door in Lowell, Massachusetts, bringing noise, fumes, dust and water mist.

item.title: Anthropic's AI model accessed US voter data: Report
item.description: Anthropic's Claude AI model bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available voter data in the U.S. state of Georgia without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday.

item.title: Some US transit systems weigh whether to run trains without a human at the controls
item.description: Even as automated vehicles such as robotaxis grow more prevalent in the U.S., almost every mass transit system still requires a driver or operator on board. Two major cities are seeking to change that.

item.title: To make AI morally good, tech companies are turning to religion. But some say it isn't that simple
item.description: As tech companies race to build the most powerful artificial intelligence, some are also asking how to teach a chatbot right from wrong. Their answer? Religion.

item.title: 'Tech debt coming due': AI-found flaw signals chaos ahead
item.description: Companies and government agencies rushed this week to patch two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language that runs a large share of the world's websites.

item.title: Engineers develop stealthy, low-cost tech to detect drones
item.description: Florida International University researchers have developed a new way to detect incoming drones using the unique magnetic signatures generated by their motors—offering a detection method that is stealthier, safer and cheaper than traditional radar.

item.title: Wearable system captures human activity data for robot training
item.description: Humanoid robots, robotic systems with a body shape that resembles that of humans, could tackle various chores and everyday manual tasks. To successfully complete these tasks, however, the robots should be able to reliably coordinate their movements, posture and how they touch or grasp different objects.

item.title: Researchers develop new way to reduce metal waste in manufacturing
item.description: Manufacturing aircraft components, battery materials, cutting tools, biomedical implants and other precision-engineered parts often involves metals in powder form.

item.title: UK pledges more funding to guard against AI risks
item.description: The U.K. government on Saturday outlined plans to expand funding for artificial intelligence safety amid growing concerns over the cyber risks posed by the increasingly advanced technology.

item.title: A timeline of developments in AI safety since the attack on Hugging Face
item.description: In one alarming announcement after another, artificial intelligence companies in recent months have shared examples of their technology acting in ways that appeared to evade instructions from humans.

item.title: Flexible robot arms learn to predict their next move
item.description: A robot arm that bends like an elephant's trunk can slip into tight spaces and handle fragile objects. Controlling it is harder because its smooth bending makes its next move hard to predict. Researchers have now developed a method that keeps computer predictions of the arm's motion on track, even when the arm moves faster than the model was trained for.

item.title: AI deepfakes are getting more realistic. Scientists developed a better way to spot them
item.description: Hundreds of the nation's computer scientists gathered for a conference in Denver last fall, and Tuan Tran had a big test for them: Could they tell the difference between the real Brad Pitt and an AI-generated version of him?

item.title: Low-power neural chip reads brain signals to identify cognitive and emotional states
item.description: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a therapeutic technique that delivers electrical pulses to specific areas of the brain via an implant to modulate neural activity. It is already widely used for movement disorders such as Parkinson's disease, and researchers are increasingly exploring its potential for severe psychiatric illnesses including major depression, posttraumatic stress disorder and obsessive-compulsive disorder.

item.title: Cation disorder could improve lithium-rich cathodes, study shows
item.description: Lithium-rich cathode materials are promising candidates for next-generation batteries, as they can store considerably more charge than materials used today in electric vehicles and electronics.

item.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence models are rooted in ideas of mid-20th-century engineers who thought some amount of irrationality was essential for a machine that could think like a human, contends Benjamin Lindquist, an assistant professor in the MIT History Section, who holds an MIT Schwarzman College of Computing shared position with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) and is a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems.

item.title: Ambient radiation used to power battery-free temperature sensor
item.description: Researchers at the University of Arkansas and the University of Michigan have reported the creation of a graphene-based energy harvester that uses ambient radiation to run ultralow-power temperature sensors. This is the second sensor created by the team whose overall goal is development of autonomous sensor systems that draw power from multiple sources in the environment—solar, thermal, acoustic, kinetic, nonlinear and ambient radiation. The findings are published in the Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B.

item.title: Curated hydrogen database reveals links between storage capacity and release pressure
item.description: Hydrogen's ability to power a cleaner future hinges not only on finding materials capable of efficiently storing and releasing it, but also on understanding the trade-off between storage capacity and practical operating conditions.

item.title: No lithium metal anode to start? Silver-based additive helps stabilize next-generation batteries
item.description: A research team at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) has developed a dynamic integrated interface engineering strategy that enhances the energy density and stability of anode-free lithium metal batteries by reconfiguring key battery interfaces.

item.title: Computer scientists build innovative tech tools to find experiments, detect citation 'hallucinations'
item.description: New York University computer scientists and students have developed a pair of web-hosted AI systems designed to increase the efficiency and accuracy of the research process—by spotting "hallucinations" in academic citations and by identifying appropriate experimental protocols for scientific studies.

item.title: Data-driven operation of biogas plants: Generating electricity when wind and solar power are scarce
item.description: Biogas plants are considered the third pillar of renewable electricity generation in Germany. Unlike solar and wind power, electricity generation from biogas is largely independent of weather conditions and can generally be scheduled.

item.title: New method produces perfect images of misaligned big toes
item.description: Patients require X-rays of their big toes before surgery. Several images are required as the development of hallux valgus needs to be monitored over time.

item.title: Musk wants to merge SpaceX and Tesla: Here's what to know
item.description: Elon Musk said this week that SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to study a merger of his two biggest companies.

item.title: Shares in this data center company are down 40% as investors lose faith in the AI story
item.description: For two decades, data centers were relatively safe, lucrative real estate investments. They attracted investors because they served as digital infrastructure—the essential plumbing that keeps the internet running.

item.title: From red mud to green concrete: Low-carbon construction material can cut carbon footprint
item.description: Research led by Trinity, in partnership with Gannon Eco and McGrath Quarries, is transforming "red mud," an industrial byproduct, into a high-performance, low-carbon construction material. The team is now moving from laboratory development to real-world industrial trials.

item.title: App's AI 'eyes' for blind users fall short, researchers find
item.description: A blind man points his phone at a pan and asks, "Are the sausages brown yet?" The app he's using responds out loud that some spots are still slightly pink. So a bit later, he takes another photo and asks again, and then again, about four times in all, until the food is fully cooked.

item.title: Molecular locking strategy enables efficient and scalable organic solar cells
item.description: Organic solar cells (OSCs) are devices that convert sunlight into electricity using carbon-based organic materials rather than the silicon used in conventional solar panels.

item.title: Doubling hydrogen production through a synergy of materials
item.description: Many chemical processes require hydrogen, which is still being produced from fossil fuels. A protonic ceramic electrolyzer cell (PCEC) is a device that can produce hydrogen from water at temperatures that match key industrial processes. Researchers at the University of Groningen recently showed that careful coordination of materials in such a PCEC can double the production of hydrogen with the same electricity consumption. The results are published in Energy and Environmental Science on Oct. 14, 2026.

item.title: Tiny 3D-printed color routers could enable sharper and brighter low-light photography
item.description: Almost every sensor in a digital photography device, from a smartphone to a digital camera, relies on color filters to separate incoming light into red, green and blue before it reaches the sensor. Substantial light is lost through the process, however, and in dim conditions, this results in images with higher noise, longer exposures and more motion blur. The most conventional configuration, a Bayer filter array, transmits only about a third of the light striking it.

item.title: Recoloring polyester with supercritical CO₂ could simplify fiber-to-fiber recycling
item.description: Colored polyester is difficult to recycle because the dyes are hard to remove without using large quantities of chemicals, water or energy. Researchers have developed a supercritical carbon dioxide treatment that redistributes existing dyes between polyester fibers, creating uniform colors without removing the original dyes. By controlling fiber proportions, they tuned shades and developed a model that accurately predicted color strength.
